utterances.text: I arrived in Prijedor after I was wounded on the 12th of September and I was there in their hospital for about ten days, that is to say, roughly until the end of September 1994.

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: All right. Now, I don't think you mentioned it in your list of locations earlier but you do mention it in your statement that you were in Trnovo in June and July of 1995. Do you recall the specific locations that you were at in Trnovo; and if you do, if you could just very briefly tell me, please.

utterances.speaker: BRANKO PREDOJEVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I can remember. With that unit that I came to as the commander of this company from the Sana Brigade that was within the joint forces of the 1st Krajina Corps under the command of then-Lieutenant-Colonel Pantelija Curguz; that is to say, I was company commander of that unit of mine because the commander of that unit went away for training. Upon arriving in the Sarajevo theatre of war, we first arrived in the village of Kijevo; that is to say, it's on that road between Trnovo and Sarajevo. From there, along this road, or rather, on the slopes above the road where that dam is on the Zeljeznica river, we arrived in the village of Ilovica. That was a smallish village, or rather, it consisted of weekend cottages. From there we crossed the road, we came to the other side, that is, and arrived at the hill of Hrastovac above that dam that I mentioned, above the Trnovo-Sarajevo road. That's where we remained for, say, 25, 6 days, that unit of my unit, that is, until our replacements came.

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: And during that time-period, were you involved in operations in respect of the Lucevik feature at all?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO PREDOJEVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. Now, as I've mentioned, you've outlined the various locations that you and your unit were in during the war period. Is it fair to say that you spent the overwhelming majority of the war period outside of Sanski Most?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO PREDOJEVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: Okay. I'd like to move now to a different topic and that relates to the command posts of the 6th Sana Brigade. Now, in paragraph 6 of your statement you talk briefly of the command post of the 6th Brigade and you say that that was located in Lusci Palanka. Now, are you aware that from the 8th of June, 1992, a forward command post was also set up by the brigade that was located in Sanski Most itself?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO PREDOJEVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: Now, this Chamber's received evidence within a combat report for the brigade, P3851, that this was the case. Now, we don't necessarily need to go to that but my question is: Do you have any reason to doubt, then, that a forward command post was set up in Sanski Most from the 8th of June, 1992?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO PREDOJEVIC
utterances.text: I don't remember that. I don't remember -- since when I came there, at that time, from Nevesinje, I went to Lusci Palanka, that is to say, where the command post was. And it is possible, as I've already said -- I mean, my memory doesn't really serve me. But later on, yes. Later on during the war - I cannot remember the exact time - the command post was moved from Lusci Palanka to Sanski Most. I think it was somewhere towards the end of that year, 1992, beginning of 1993, something like that. I cannot say for sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: And if I told you that the same document, the combat report of the 6th Brigade for 1992, said that the command of the -- the permanent command of the brigade did move from Lusci Palanka to Sanski Most on the -- at the end of August 1992, would that perhaps refresh your recollection?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO PREDOJEVIC
utterances.text: I've already said that I spent most of the time -- actually, particularly the first part of the war outside of Sanski Most, or rather, at my own battalion command that was in the area of the villages from which I obtained personnel -- well, it didn't really help me remember. I cannot say exactly what the time was.

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: Okay. That's understood. Thank you. I'd like to move on to a different topic, one that's -- you've already testified about briefly today and that's the SOS unit that was in Sanski Most. Now, in paragraph 6 of your statement you mention Colonel Anicic and you say that he and Dane Ergarac were in command of the SOS. Now, Nedjeljko Anicic was the commander of the Serbian TO after it was set up in February 1992; correct?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO PREDOJEVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: Now, you say in paragraph 6 as amended today that -- as corrected today, that the SOS participated in the liberation of the Municipal Assembly building in Sanski Most. Now, they also participated in combat operations, mop-up operations in Sanski Most at the end of May and early June 1992; correct?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO PREDOJEVIC
utterances.text: Yes. This happened before I arrived in Sanski Most and before I was deployed in the 6th Sana Brigade, but I heard that things were exactly as you had put it just now.

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: And you also heard that when conducting these operations at the end of May and early June 1992, the SOS were acting in co-ordination with the 6th Brigade; correct?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO PREDOJEVIC
utterances.text: Well, I don't know that they were acting in co-ordination because until they joined my unit, they worked according to some plan of theirs or Anicic's or Dane Ergarac and his deputy, so you couldn't make head or tails out of it, as we say. And then they became part of my battalion.

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: Now, the operations that you have said that the SOS were participating in at the end of May and early June, would you agree with me that they were in Mahala, Vrhpolje, and Hrustovo, among other locations?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO PREDOJEVIC
utterances.text: As for these villages that you are referring to and Mahala, part of Sanski Most, I just heard about these things that happened. And I assume that they probably did take part but I doubt that they had any kind of co-ordination or that they were under the command of the 6th Sana. Because I've already said that these were young men who were not disciplined, who acted on their own when carrying out tasks, and even when they would receive a concrete order, again they would do things their way, in their own interest?

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: So leaving aside issues then of co-ordination or command, would you agree with me that the 6th Brigade were also at the same locations that the SOS were found at the end of May and early June, including Mahala, Hrustovo, and Vrhpolje?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO PREDOJEVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I agree on that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Jeremy, by locations, do you mean operations in fact?

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. Thank you for that clarification.

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: And, Witness, just to be fair to you, I meant that the 6th Brigade were involved in the same operations that the SOS were involved in in Hrustovo, Mahala, and Vrhpolje.

utterances.speaker: BRANKO PREDOJEVIC
utterances.text: I've already said that they could take part at the same time, but in co-ordination, that's what I doubt. I wasn't there, as I've already said, but I know these people and even when they came to my unit, it took me a while to try to turn them into soldiers. Until then they were totally dishevelled, if I can put it that way, and they worked and operated any which way they wanted.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Are you talking about your -- those soldiers or are you talking about those who commanded that operation?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In this case I'm talking about these soldiers, the members of the Serb Defence Forces.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, but when you say you doubt whether it's in co-ordination, it could still have been co-ordinated, wouldn't it, and then perhaps the soldiers might not have behaved as they were expected to do, but that doesn't make co-ordination at the command level in any way impossible? Or would you disagree?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't agree with that, knowing these men, that they could accept command just like that from someone who was not part of their own plans as to how they should operate. That's how they behaved all the time until they became part of that same 6th Sana Brigade. They left whenever they wanted to go and in numbers that they wanted, irrespective of --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Witness, you continue again to explain to us what you are not specifically asked for. It appears to me that you haven't addressed the matter I asked you, but I'll not insist and invite Mr. Jeremy to continue.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Just before Mr. Jeremy continues, just to remind you that Mr. Jeremy's question was: Did these SOS members participate in the same operations as the unit of the army even though they may not have been doing so in co-ordination with the army? So don't -- if you answer the question, don't keep going back to "co-ordination." The question is: They were in the same operation?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] According to the information that I had, they did take part in some of these actions; however, which ones specifically and how many of them took part, that I really cannot say.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: That was not the question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: Witness, just to stay with this topic, did you ever have any personal conversations with brigade-level staff, with Colonel Basara, for example, about whether or not the 6th Brigade was co-ordinating with the SOS during these May/June operations?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO PREDOJEVIC
utterances.text: I did not talk to Colonel Basara. I never talked to him about these activities. I was just a battalion commander and I arrived later. So we really didn't have time to talk about any of that and no need to either.

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: That's understood. Now, you've mentioned that the SOS -- members of the SOS unit became part of your battalion in 1993 and you discuss this in your statement, for example, in paragraph 13. Now, one of those members of the SOS that joined your battalion was a man called Zoran Ilic; correct?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO PREDOJEVIC
utterances.text: I cannot remember all members of this unit , or rather, the SOS, whether this Ilic was there too. But around 30 of these members became part of my unit on the 7th of April, when we were getting ready and when we went to the Bihac front.

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: Okay. I'd like to show you a document relating to this man to see if it refreshes your recollection about whether he was in your unit.

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: Could we please see 65 ter 31869.

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: Now, sir, on the screen before you is a letter from the command of the 3rd Battalion, 6th Brigade, location Dzevar. It's dated the 13th of May, 1993. The title is: Zeljko Ilic, explanation. And, sir, having read "Zeljko Ilic" to myself, I've realised that I asked you if you know a Zoran Ilic. So I will correct myself and ask if you knew a Zeljko Ilic? Sir, you'll have an opportunity to read the letter. My question is --

utterances.speaker: BRANKO PREDOJEVIC
utterances.text: Zeljko Ilic?

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: Do you recall this man?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO PREDOJEVIC
utterances.text: You said the 1st Battalion but this is my battalion, the 3rd one, the 3rd Battalion. And I signed this, or who was this that signed on my behalf? Somebody signed, one of my people. I cannot see exactly who it was. The signature is illegible. It's possible that it was Veljko Stupar, he was desk officer for general affairs.

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: And I understand that it would be typical that as a battalion commander persons would occasionally sign documents such as these on your behalf; correct?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO PREDOJEVIC
utterances.text: That was not the rule. That was not the rule, but if at that time I was somewhere in the field outside Sanski Most and the command with two persons functioned throughout the war and they issued all sorts of certificates, compiled lists, did administrative work of that kind, who had left and so on and so forth.

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: Okay. Now, I'm not sure if you've answered the question, but do you -- having looked at this letter, do you recall Zeljko Ilic?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO PREDOJEVIC
utterances.text: Well, I cannot remember every member. I mean, over a thousand of them went through my unit --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Not every member, Witness.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] -- so I was practically a stranger there --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: You're not being asked to remember all. You're being asked whether you remember this one. Do you or do you not remember this particular person?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, I'm not sure. I cannot remember this man specifically.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: Now, Witness, let's take a look at this letter. So we see in the first paragraph there is a reference to Zeljko Ilic, we see his address. We read that he has been a member of the SOS, Serbian Defence Forces, since the 10th of March, 1992, and we read that that unit has been subordinated to this battalion since the 1st of April, 1993. Now going to the third paragraph, we read that Zeljko Ilic has participated in all combat carried out by his units, especially combat in Krupa na Uni, the mopping up of Sanski Most and Kljuc, and in operations to spear-head a corridor through to Serbia. Those mopping-up operations that we see here, that's a reference to the mopping-up operations I asked you about earlier at the end of May and early June; correct?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO PREDOJEVIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes, that's when those actions took place.

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: Okay. And that same third paragraph reads on to say: "During all this combat, he exhibited exemplary courage, daring, and discipline when carrying out his command and the other tasks."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: His combat, not command.

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: Sorry, excuse me, thank you for the correction.

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: "... when carrying out his combat and other tasks." Sir, in respect to the mopping-up operations that Zeljko Ilic and the SOS unit were involved in, the -- in respect to those operations at the end of May and early June, this Chamber has received evidence of an incident that occurred on Vrhpolje bridge during these mopping-up operations, specifically on the 31st of May, 1992. At that time soldiers rounded up the Muslim inhabitants of Begici near Vrhpolje. They took the men to Vrhpolje bridge. They beat them, forced them to jump off of the bridge, and as they fell into the water they were shot with automatic weapons. I take it that you are aware of this incident; yes?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO PREDOJEVIC
utterances.text: As for this incident, I heard about that upon my arrival in the unit. What happened exactly and who did what -- I mean, since I was not there in Sanski Most at the time, I really wouldn't have anything to say about the matter.

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: And did you hear that this man, Zeljko Ilic, was among the Serb soldiers at the bridge in Vrhpolje on the 31st of May? And I can tell you that that is evidence that this Trial Chamber has received, a statement, P2502. So were you aware that Zeljko Ilic was on this Vrhpolje bridge on the 31st of May, 1992?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO PREDOJEVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: Going back to this letter, we see in the second paragraph that there is an explanation or recommendation in order to sort out the rights of Zeljko Ilic regarding the use of a motor vehicle that he purchased from Ismet Kurbegovic of Sanski Most. Now, is that name, Ismet Kurbegovic, familiar to you, sir?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO PREDOJEVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: Now, there's also evidence in this case at transcript page 2151-2152 that Ismet Kurbegovic -- or an Ismet Kurbegovic was killed next to Vrhpolje bridge on the 31st of May, 1992, by a man called Jadranko Palija. Now, I have two focused questions in respect of this. The first one is: Do you know if the Ismet Kurbegovic here, referred to in this letter, is the same man that was killed on Vrhpolje bridge?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO PREDOJEVIC
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: And my next question is: Do you know a Jadranko Palija? Is that a name that is familiar to you?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO PREDOJEVIC
utterances.text: No. There were a few of these Ilics in my unit, but this one, no, not in SOS, not in my unit, no, at least not in that part of the SOS that joined my unit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The question is about Palija not Ilic.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't know him.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: Now I would like to show you a document in connection with Jadranko Palija.

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: But before I do, I would like to tender the document on the screen before us.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document 31869 receives Exhibit Number P7071, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: Thank you. Could we please see 65 ter 31801.

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: Now, sir, coming up on the screen before you or on the screen before you is a confirmation of military service of Jadranko Palija. It's dated the 24th of June, 1994.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: I think it's Palija. You said Palaja.

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour, Palija.

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: Sir, as a battalion commander I take it you're familiar with the form of the certificate on the screen before us?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO PREDOJEVIC
utterances.text: I personally did not issue such certificates. This is a certificate issued by the brigade command.

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: And we see the certificate is dated the 24th of June, 1994, and it indicates that Private Jadranko Palija was in War Unit 8099 from the 13th of November, 1991, until the 13th of July, 1993. Sir, are you familiar with or do you still remember what this reference to War Unit 8099 indicates?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO PREDOJEVIC
utterances.text: That was a war unit of the 6th Krajina Brigade while it was still in Jasenovac, as far as I can remember. I see that this is a stamp of military post 7421, that is the military post of the 6th Sana Brigade, that is to say, when it arrived in Sanski Most and when I was a member of that brigade.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Predojevic, may I ask you: Are you familiar with this man, Jadranko Palija?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Earlier on the gentleman was saying Prljaja, if I remember correctly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: That is exactly --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] As for Palija --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Go ahead.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Palija I remember because of this characteristic surname, yes, yes. He was part of the unit but he certainly wasn't with me, with my unit. And he was not in the SOS forces.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Perhaps you -- if there's a need for you should clarify that because earlier you referred again to the name Palaja.

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: Thank you for that intervention, Your Honour, it's appreciated.

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: Now --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could I also ask one question. Do you have any recollection of that person apart from recognising the name? Do you have a vague recollection of that person?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I didn't know him that well, but I remember now when I read this Palija, I remember that he was there -- I mean, but who he was exactly and which unit he belonged to exactly, that I cannot recall.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, you apparently remember that he was not in the SOS forces.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I said the forces that came to join my unit, that soldier was not on that force. Now, whether he was part of their unit before that and then when these people joined me, whether he went somewhere else, that I don't know. But he certainly wasn't one of those that joined me on the 7th of April when we set out for the Bihac front.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Now, could you tell me, was this a man of 20-years-old, 30-years-old, 40-years-old, 50 -- approximate age, could you tell us at the time?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think he was a youngish man. I cannot remember exactly, I cannot remember his face, Palija. I seem to remember a big man, dark-haired, not older than 25.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Jeremy, perhaps I bring it to your attention that the date of birth given for this person in this document, at least in the English version - the original might be different - raises some questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: Now, sir, having refreshed your recollection who this Jadranko Palija might have been, do you recall whether he was involved -- whether you heard that he was involved in operations on Vrhpolje bridge at the end of May 1992?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO PREDOJEVIC
utterances.text: No, I don't know about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: And, Your Honours, in respect to the date I'll ask for a revision of the English. To me it looks like 1961.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, at least 61 is almost as good as 81, I would say that's -- but --

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: Your Honours --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We'll leave it to that.

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We're not going to -- well, of course we have to interpret the evidence but to say, well, I just ask for 81 to be changed into 61, that's perhaps a bit too quick.

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: Yeah, understood, Your Honours. And there are also other ways I think I can verify this date which I won't go into now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, it's only a year, by the way, but there are perhaps other ways of verifying that, that may cause this to be interpreted in the way as you suggested.

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: Now, coming back to this document, Witness, we see that it outlines the period of time that he was in the -- this war unit, 8099. And it also records that no criminal proceedings are being conducted against this particular man as of the 24th of June, 1994. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO PREDOJEVIC
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, I can see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: Now, as a follow-up question to that, are you aware that criminal proceedings were subsequently conducted against a man called Jadranko Palija and that in 2008 he was sentenced by the BH state court to 28 years for a crime committed during the war, including for his role in the Vrhpolje bridge massacre? Was that something you were aware of?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO PREDOJEVIC
utterances.text: I'm not aware of that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Witness --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In 1999 I was reassigned to the --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Witness --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] -- Novi Sad command, therefore I stopped following the developments over there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Witness, if you say "I'm not aware," you've answered the question. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: Could I tender that document, please, as the next Prosecution exhibit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document 31801 receives Exhibit Number P7072, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: P7072 is admitted into evidence, but I immediately observe in relation to this that the translation -- the accuracy of the translation is not thereby yet established.

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: Just to close this line of questioning, sir, I'd like to show you one final exhibit.

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: Could we please see 65 ter 31900.

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: Now, sir, just coming up on your -- on the screen before you is a --

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: Could we go to the second page in one of these documents. Thanks.

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: It's a press release from the court of Bosnia and Herzegovina taken from the web site of that court.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: The English disappeared ... that's again B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: Yeah, we have it now. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: Now, sir, in this press release we read that the appellate panel confirmed the verdict in the Jadranko Palija case. And we read in the first paragraph that the --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: You always say Palaja. You mean Palija, I think.

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: I do, Your Honours, and hopefully that will be the last time you need to correct me. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: Sir, in respect to Jadranko Palija, we see that the appellate panel confirmed the verdict in that case and that the panel of the appellate division of the court of Bosnia and Herzegovina found Jadranko Palija guilty of war crimes against humanity and war crimes against civilians and imposed on him a sentence of 28 years of long-term imprisonment. And we see in the second paragraph some details about the verdict. And we read in the first sentence that he was found guilty because: "On the 31st of May, 1992, together with other soldiers of the VRS, he took part in an attack against the hamlet of Begici, the village of Kljevci, on which occasion they rounded up all the civilians found there ..." It goes on to say that they separated the men from the women and children. And in the last -- just to summarise, in the last sentences we read that he killed one more civilian on the main road leading to Sanski Most and he killed a civilian on Vrhpolje bridge, and together with other soldiers he participated in the killing of 14 civilians who were ordered to remove their clothes and jump off the bridge while being fired at as they were falling into the water. And I finish it there. So seeing that press release from the BH state court, does that refresh your recollection at all? I realise if you haven't seen it, then it won't refresh it, but I ask you the question.

utterances.speaker: BRANKO PREDOJEVIC
utterances.text: At the beginning of my testimony I said that I joined the Sana Most [as interpreted] Brigade on the 26th of June, 1992. I heard of this case but I don't know any details.

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: Your Honours, I'd like to tender that as the next Prosecution exhibit.

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: If the Defence wants to make its stipulation on the record in respect of this, then I won't insist --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Stipulation of what, Mr. -- that this judgement was delivered, is that what you're talking about, or that he committed those crimes, Mr. Palija?

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: That this judgement was delivered.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Delivered. Would you -- Mr. Stojanovic, is there any dispute about this judgement having been delivered and that it covered the charges and that Mr. Palija was convicted for those charges?

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I will always stipulate with the Prosecutor that this type of decision was made. I am familiar with the case. I know that the case was brought to the Constitutional Court of Bosnia and Herzegovina, but the decision is being reconsidered. I agree that Jadranko Palija was found guilty and that the appeals court confirmed his 20-year imprisonment sentence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And also that the judgement covered the facts as read out by Mr. Jeremy and appearing in the press release.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I wouldn't be able to stipulate that, Your Honour. I'm not that familiar with the case. I can only confirm the fact that he was convicted and sentenced to 20 years in prison.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And did that include the event at the Vrhpolje bridge?

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, that is part of the decision, I can confirm that and I can agree with that. Now, as to whether the things had transpired in that way, I wouldn't be able to tell you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It's a little bit unclear to me what you mean by "whether the things had transpired in that way." I do not know what way and I do not know what had transpired. So therefore it's ...

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I mean the text provided by the court of Bosnia and Herzegovina because this gives us what the verdict reads. I can agree with the wording of the verdict, but whether things happened in that way or not, I don't know, because he is still fighting for the truth and who am I to interfere with that?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Stojanovic, if you would have carefully listened to Mr. Jeremy, you would have known that he sought a stipulation on this judgement being delivered, not on the truth of its content. So therefore, you're responding to something which is not -- which is not apparently the cas. Madam Registrar, would you please --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: May I first ask Mr. Stojanovic, you referred to a sentence of 20 years, but in this press release it is stated that this person was convicted for 28 years. Was it in -- did you misspeak?

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't think that I misspoke. Yes, I agree that he was sentenced to 28 years in prison. I believe that that's what I said the first time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar, the Chamber in view of the fact that there was no clear stipulation, the Chamber admits the document into evidence. Could you please assign a number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document 31900 receives Exhibit Number P7073, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: P7073 is admitted. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: And, sir, a final question on this area. Now, according to evidence in this case, Colonel Basara was at the location of the Vrhpolje bridge at some point on the 31st of May, 1992. Now, are you aware of any steps that Colonel Basara took to discipline or punish any members of the 6th Brigade or the SOS in respect to the events that happened on Vrhpolje bridge on the 31st of May, 1992?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO PREDOJEVIC
utterances.text: I don't know if any measures were taken.

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: I think we're at break time, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We are at break time. We'll take a break and we would like to see you back in 20 minutes from now because we resume at 25 minutes to 2.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: While we are waiting for the witness to enter the courtroom, P6938 was marked for identification on the 24th of November of last year pending an agreement between the parties as to whether tendering 80 pages of the document was necessary. This can be found at transcript page 28735 to 736. On the 18th of December, the Prosecution informed the Chamber via e-mail that it would only like to tender an excerpt from P6938 consisting of pages 1 through 8 of the English translation and pages 1 through 6 of the B/C/S version and that the Defence does not object. I take it that this is reliable information we received. The Chamber admits into evidence pages 1 through 8 of the English version of P6938 and pages 1 through 6 of the B/C/S version of P6938. And the Prosecution is instructed to upload a new version of P6938 reflecting the Chamber's decision and the Registry is instructed to make the necessary replacement thereafter.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Jeremy.

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: Now -- so I'm going to do my best to finish my questions today and I'd like to begin this session by talking to you about the Gvozden case which you've already mentioned during your direct examination and which you refer to in your statement. And now you've -- a criminal report that Colonel Basara filed in respect to this case has been tendered today, that's D882. And I'd like to look at an exhibit in connection with this, a different exhibit, which is P3823. And while it's coming up, sir, I can tell you it's a regular combat report from the 1st Krajina Corps and it's dated the 6th of December, 1992, so that is -- that's the day, a day after Basara's report, D882. Could we go to page -- let's just quickly look. So it's from the 1st Krajina Corps command, 6 December 1992, and it's to the Main Staff of the Army of Republika Srpska and we see it's a combat report.

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: Could we go to the second page, please, in each language.

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: Now, sir, under number 5 we see the subheading: "Unusual incidents." And we read, and I paraphrase, that on the 5th of December, 1992, five men in uniform, probably members of the 6th Light Infantry Brigade, killed seven and wounded one Croatian civilian in the villages of Tomasica and Sasina. And we read that there were three women among those killed. Going to the next paragraph we read that the killings were committed by a still unidentified group of people. It is known that a man called Gvozden was a member of that group. It is assumed that the motive for the killings was revenge because according to witnesses, Gvozden's brother was killed on the front a couple of days ago. And it finishes by saying investigation is underway and the results will be sent to you. So this is a reference to the same incident that was referred to in Basara's report; correct?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO PREDOJEVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: And were you aware that this particular incident was reported to the Main Staff by the 1st Krajina Corps?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO PREDOJEVIC
utterances.text: No. As the battalion commander, I didn't know that.

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: I'd like to look at a connected document.

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: Could we please see 65 ter 07057.

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: And, sir, while that's being brought up I can tell you it's a decision by the Banja Luka Military Court to remand into custody Mile Gvozden and others under suspicion of having committed murder of Croat civilians in the village of Sasina. The document is on the screen before us now. We see it's dated the 17th of December, 1992. We see there's a description of the investigation and we see that there is a ruling.

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: Could we go to the next page in the English, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: So, sir, there we see --

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: And could we go to the next page in the B/C/S as well, please -- actually, sorry, stay with the B/C/S page. Forgive me.

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: So we see a description of the crime. That's the same crime that -- that's described in Basara's report; correct?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO PREDOJEVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: And could we go to the next page in the English and the B/C/S, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: And we see a ruling, it's just -- it's above the signature in the B/C/S and it's at the bottom of the page in the English, we see: "By ruling of this court number 103/92 of 6 December 1992, the accused are hereby remanded in custody for a period of one month, pursuant to Article 191, paragraph 1 of the Law on Criminal Procedure." So, sir, I think you mentioned that you were aware that these men were brought into custody. This ruling, I take it, is consistent with your recollection of events?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO PREDOJEVIC
utterances.text: As far as I can remember now, I believe that that was the case, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: I'd tender that document as the next Prosecution exhibit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document 07057 receives Exhibit P7074, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: Could we please see 07063.

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: And, sir, we're on the same topic, this is a decision from the Banja Luka Military Court and it's dated the 2nd of January, 1993. So we see in the first paragraph -- or we see the document is from the Banja Luka Military Court. We see the date, 2nd of January, 1993. We see a reference to the Gvozden case in the first paragraph and we see a ruling stating that: "Custody of the following accused ceased ..." And four men with the last name Gvozden are listed.

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: Could we please go to the second page in the English.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: But in the English you should read the final sentence after the names in that paragraph: "The accused shall be released immediately."

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: And so we see a reference there saying the accused shall be released immediately. So I'd like to focus on the words beginning with "on the 2nd of January, 1993," where we read: "On the 2nd of January, 1993, the investigating judge questioned the accused, who stated that they wanted to return to their unit and proposed to that the court end their custody. "The investigating judge considered the proposal of the accused and found that the reason for remanding them custody as stipulated under Article 191, paragraph 1 of the ZKP, Law on Criminal Procedure, pursuant to which the accused were remanded in custody, no longer existed. The military prosecutor also agreed with the cessation of custody and I therefore issued the ruling herein." So, sir, I take it from your earlier testimony that this is also consistent with your recollection that these men were released back into your unit shortly after they were brought into custody; correct?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO PREDOJEVIC
utterances.text: Yes, but I did not know that they had been remanded in custody. I remember Mile very well and I know that he rejoined the unit.

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: I'd like to tender that document as the next Prosecution exhibit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Excuse me. Document 07063 receives Exhibit P7075, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: Now, sir, I'd like to finish this line of questioning by showing -- well, first by asking you a question. Were you aware that in 1999 proceedings in this case were still ongoing?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO PREDOJEVIC
utterances.text: No, I was not aware of that.

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: Could we please take a look at 65 ter 31872.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Jeremy, have you sought to agree with the Defence on the follow-up in this case, where the witness apparently does not have much knowledge and where there is documentary evidence? I mean, the easiest way is to agree this is the course it took and then to present those documents from the bar table or in whatever way.

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: I haven't done that, Your Honour. I'm happy to skip this document and sit with Mr. Stojanovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Of course, you should do that before you start your cross-examination preferably if there's any matter, but let's move on because -- unless, Mr. Stojanovic, you would agree that all the documentary evidence by Mr. Jeremy is -- reflects the course of -- that the proceedings took after 1992? What other documents do you have or is this the only one?

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: This is the final document I was intending to use, this is the latest document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then perhaps it takes more time to seek an agreement. Then let's move on.

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: Sir, very quickly we see this is a letter from the Republika Srpska Military Court in Banja Luka. We see it's dated the 24th of November, 1999, and we see that it's to the Ministry of Justice of Republika Srpska. The body of the text outlines the history of the events in the Gvozden case to date.

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: If we could go to the second page in the English, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: And we see that in the final paragraph we read that: "Since we have received no information as to whether the request for extradition was filed," and that's a reference to extradition of Gvozden, "and if it was filed whether the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia agreed to extradite the accused, we hereby request relevant information so that we can continue the criminal proceedings." So, sir, would you agree that on the basis of this letter criminal proceedings had still not been concluded in respect to this Gvozden case by the 24th of November, 1999?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO PREDOJEVIC
utterances.text: Yes, obviously.

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: I tender that document, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document 31872 receives Exhibit Number P7076, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Admitted into evidence. The appropriate course to take under those circumstances, Mr. Jeremy, is the following: If you see in the statement that the criminal report filed by Colonel Basara is an associated exhibit, then you should approach the Defence and say: I wish to inform the Chamber about that follow-up of that case, I have three, four documents about that because this witness isn't aware of all the documents. And then to propose to the Defence that you would agree that these were the steps taken subsequent to what the Defence presented in its associated exhibits. That's the most efficient way of dealing with it and I would urge the parties to more often use those ways to agree. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: Now, sir, I'd like to discuss paragraph 17 of your statement, where you refer to overlaps between the VRS and the Crisis Staff. Now, did you personally attend Crisis Staff meetings?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO PREDOJEVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: Now, can we agree that as someone who didn't attend Crisis Staff meetings and as someone who spent the overwhelming majority of the war period outside of Sanski Most, you're not really in a position to provide evidence about overlaps between the Crisis Staff and the 6th Brigade and what was actually discussed at those meetings?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO PREDOJEVIC
utterances.text: I agree.

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: Thank you. Now I'd like to move on to the topic of departure of non-Serbs from Sanski Most. Now, in paragraph 16 of your statement we read that: The VRS was never involved in any removal of the civilian population from Sanski Most and the VRS had nothing to do with it. We only carried out military tasks. Now, again, as someone who spent the overwhelming majority of the war period outside of Sanski Most, can we agree that you are not able to provide evidence on what the VRS was doing in respect to removal of the civilian population for those periods that you were not in Sanski Most?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO PREDOJEVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I agree. I arrived on the 22nd of June, 1992. I've already said that several times. So I agree with you.

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: Now, as a final area, I'd like to focus on Trnovo which you refer to in paragraph 21 of your statement. Now, in that paragraph you say you headed to Trnovo on the 20th of June, 1995, you spent about 20 days there. You say: "I did not see volunteers from Serbia nor did any such volunteers from Serbia take part in the action conducted by the VRS against the forces of the ABiH in the territory of Trnovo municipality." Now, sir, when you refer to volunteers from Serbia, who exactly are you referring to?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO PREDOJEVIC
utterances.text: I'm not referring to anybody in particular. I as a company commander who was up there in the forest some 20 kilometres from Trnovo could only learn as much. At that time I did not hear of any unit being deployed there.

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: So, sir, I understand that your evidence is that there were no units from Serbia in the areas in Trnovo that you were in during the period in your statement; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO PREDOJEVIC
utterances.text: No, I do not exclude the possibility that they were there. I'm just saying that I didn't know of their deployment because I was with my men on the first line all that time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Witness, may I take you to what was just read to you. Your statement says you didn't see the volunteers. That's clear, you didn't see them from Serbia. "... nor did any such volunteers from Serbia take part in the action conducted by the VRS against the forces of the ABiH in the territory of Trnovo municipality." As a matter of fact, you are telling us now: I didn't see them and I don't know whether there were any. Is that well understood?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, well understood. Where I was on the front line and as much as I could hear from my neighbours, they were not there. But I really can't say that they were not there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Now, instead of changing tiny little thing -- dates in your statement, it would have been better if you would have, when you were prepared for this evidence, you should have said: This is not true that they were not there because I do not know. That's what you were expected to do during proofing. Because in your statement, what you say in your statement is clearly contradicted now by what you are telling us; that is, that you do not know whether Serbian volunteers participated in Trnovo operations. Mr. Jeremy.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: And I would like to add, the same is true for your statement in paragraphs 16 and 17 of your statement which is now contradicted by your evidence that you were not aware, you didn't know about it, because you were most of the time absent from that region.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Mr. Jeremy.

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: And thank you, Witness, I have no further questions. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Jeremy. Mr. Stojanovic, any questions in re-examination? Please be aware that we have to conclude not one second later than quarter past 2.00.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, Your Honours, no questions for this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then this concludes your evidence, Mr. Predojevic. We'd like to thank you very much for coming a long way to The Hague and for having answered all the questions that were put to you, put to you by the parties and by the Bench. And I wish you a safe return home again. You may follow the usher.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The last few questions and answers and observations by the Bench triggered the following observation, Mr. Stojanovic. Of course the witness should have corrected the statement, but a cautious taking of a statement would have prevented that those sweeping statements on matters the witness just doesn't know should never have entered into those statements. We have ten minutes left. I do not know whether the next witness is stand-by or whether we would -- otherwise, the next witness is not stand-by, then we'll use the time for a few matters from the ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, there's one short item. We received a short report on expert witnesses last week. Mr. Lukic, the Chamber again emphasises that what we need is expert reports to be filed and to be presented. Then I'd like to deal with - let me just have a look - with the use of resources in bringing Borislav Vasiljevic to The Hague. On the 23rd of January, after having been informed by the Prosecution that it would not cross-examine Witness Borislav Vasiljevic, the Chamber instructed the Defence to postpone calling the witness to give testimony in The Hague until further notice. The Chamber felt that the Defence should make an effort to avoid a situation where resources are spent by bringing a witness to The Hague solely for a Rule 92 ter attestation. The Chamber also considered that any additional evidence the Defence wishes to elicit from the witness in court could have been included in the statement itself. From a review of the statement, the Chamber could not discern that the witness's evidence related to the acts and conduct of the accused and further wondered more generally what this witness evidence could add to the case. The Chamber hereby instructs the Defence to consider how to proceed with this witness and to inform the Chamber no later than the 9th of February of this year. I now continue briefly with an issue remaining from the testimony of Tomislav Puhalac. On the 10th of November of last year, the Chamber marked Exhibit D759 for identification pending verification of its translation, and that can be found at transcript page 28030. On the 3rd of December, the Chamber followed up with the Defence via an e-mail on the status of the requested translation. The Defence responded the same day and advised that the discrepancy noted in court were in relation to the two versions of the original. As such, CLSS is not able to change the original. However, as the Defence discovered another discrepancy, it submitted a request for verification to CLSS. On the 16th of December of last year, the Chamber followed up again via e-mail on the progress of this requested translation. As of today's date, the Chamber has not received a response. Is the Defence now in a position to update the Chamber on it at this stage?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I'm not, Your Honour. I have to check with --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: -- my Case Manager.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- then we'll hear from you tomorrow first in the morning. Then one more item, but we'll finish exact in time, is about the Dobrovoljacka Street incident recording. On the 1st of September, 2014, during the testimony of Milorad Bukva, the Chamber asked the Prosecution to inquire whether any audio recordings or written transcripts of communication preceding the Dobrovoljacka Street incident existed. This can be found at transcript pages 25004 through 006. On the 29th of October, the Prosecution advised the Chamber via e-mail that it had limited information that there may be an audio recording held in the military court in Belgrade. On the 27th of November, the Prosecution indicated that it did not have any specific knowledge whether efforts to obtain a copy of the recording were under way. This can be found at transcript pages 28947 to 948. The Chamber hereby instructs the Prosecution to explore whether it is possible to obtain a copy of the recording and the Chamber -- and inform the Chamber should a copy be retrieved. I leave it to that. We adjourn for the day and we'll resume tomorrow, Thursday, the 29th of January, 9.30 in the morning, in this same courtroom, I.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Thursday, the 29th day of January, 2015, at 9.30 a.m. 24 25
